newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Singapore PM signs Cambodian investment pact.
newsitem.headline: Singapore PM signs Cambodian investment pact.

text.p: Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong arrived in Cambodia on Monday for a two-day state visit focusing on business ties between the two nations.

Goh, who was greeted at the airport by Cambodian co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen, presided over the signing of a bilateral investment pact and air link agreement, as well as the opening of a $46 million Singaporean brewery.
"This has so far been a very successful visit," said Cambodian Minister of Foreign Affairs Ung Huot.
Officials said the investment protection and promotion agreement will protect Singaporean companies against any possible future nationalisation of the industry and allow free transfer of profits.
The bilateral airways agreement will formalise air links between the two nations, said Vichit Ith, chairman of Cambodia's flag carrier, Royal Air Cambodge (RAC).

A Cambodian foreign affairs official said the pact would likely lead to an increase in flights between the two nations, but Vichit Ith said both RAC and Silk Air of Singapore would have to study the economics of adding flights before planning any increase in service.

After signing the pacts, Goh attended opening ceremonies at Cambodia Brewery Ltd, a joint venture company between Asia Pacific Breweries Ltd of Singapore and Progress Import and Export Co Ltd of Cambodia.
The plant, which will produce Tiger and Anchor beers as well as ABC stout, has a brewing capacity of 17 million litres and cost $46 million, according to a company statement.

Rick Linck, general manager of Cambodia Brewery, told Goh and the Cambodian co-premiers that their attendance at the ceremony showed "their personal interest in investments done by way of joint ventures between companies from both countries."
Goh is scheduled to leave Cambodia on Tuesday, after his business delegation attends a seminar hosted by the Ministry of Economy and Finance.
Goh is the first Singaporean prime minister to visit Cambodia since 1968, officials said.
